⚠️ CPU card high-risk mode: incorrect PIN/APDU may lock the card

You are using AECardTools raw tunnel mode. This mode allows raw instructions to be sent directly to the card.

1. Permanent card damage risk (Brick Risk)
 • For CPU cards (IsoDep), incorrect APDU commands, especially PIN verification related ones, may cause permanent lockout.

2. Phone hardware safety statement
 • This tool only uses official Android standard APIs.
 • In theory it should not damage the phone NFC chip, but high-frequency operations may generate heat.

3. Legal responsibility
 • The user is responsible for every instruction sent.

You are performing raw NfcA passthrough operations.

1. Block 0 write risk
 • A wrong BCC can immediately brick the card irreversibly.

2. Backdoor command risk
 • Backdoor commands such as 40/43 behave differently across card vendors and may require a power cycle retry.

3. UFUID lock is irreversible
 • Once locked, backdoor capability is lost.
Raw protocol passthrough sends the byte stream directly to the card. Use it only in authorized test environments.

• Writing incorrect data to Block 0 can turn the card into a silent brick that no reader can recognize again (irreversible)\n• For AEFS cards, damaging key blocks will make all data undecryptable\n• For magic cards (UFUID), a locking operation cannot be reversed
• Once written, original data will be completely overwritten and cannot be recovered\n• NFC communication interruptions may result in incomplete writes and data corruption
